Good point — agreed the original wording was too strong. I have softened the sentence as follows:

Was: "Our study confirms that reported improvements in the survival of critically ill patients with cancer extend to the sub-group with neutropenia and sepsis or septic shock."

Now: "Our findings are consistent with the possibility that the reported improvements in survival of critically ill patients with cancer may also extend to the sub-group with neutropenia and sepsis or septic shock, although our study was not designed to test this directly."

Specifically: "confirms ... extend" → "our findings are consistent with the possibility that ... may also extend", and I added a clause making clear that our study was not designed to test this directly, so the claim is framed as a hypothesis-generating observation rather than confirmation.
